A1.justification: v2 explicitly extends v1's L2RW benchmark. Both PDFs are readable, including their equations, tables, figures and end matter. All supplied pages were inspected; neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-based retrieval experiments under CI, EI and ES, together with component ablations and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original image experiments and adds video retrieval experiments, component ablations, adversarial and corruption evaluations, and gradient-inversion results.

M1.justification: The original DPPT is retained as I-DPPT. V-DPPT adds a limited procedural adaptation: sampling video sequences and averaging normalized frame embeddings before classification and MRB processing (Section III-D). The encoder, losses, memory mechanism and federated aggregation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 retains SYSU-MM01, RegDB and LLCM, and adds video retrieval on HITSZ-VCM and BUPTCampus, including transfer between those datasets. It also introduces corrupted-input, adversarial and gradient-leakage test scenarios absent from v1.

E2.justification: The original image comparator sets are retained. v2 adds centralized image comparisons including HOSNet, DSAF and FDNM (Table III), and video comparisons including AuxNet, MITML, CLIP-ReID, TF-CLIP and VLD (Tables V–VI). DNS also becomes the comparator for robustness and reconstruction evaluations.

E3.justification: Existing image settings remain stable. New video protocols specify six- or ten-frame sequences, dataset-specific batches, 100 training epochs and additional rank-5/rank-20 reporting. Video 'EI' uses camera-partitioned training on one source dataset and tests another, whereas image EI trains across two source entities. New attack and reconstruction procedures further expand evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds video component ablations, cross-client MRB alignment analysis, cosine-similarity matrices, adversarial/corruption tests and an iDLG reconstruction case study. The original lambda/top-K sweeps remain. However, the Euclidean and mixed-distance MRB-loss ablations in v1 Table 3 are removed.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.1 states that all reported results are repeated ten times. v2 omits this statement and supplies no replacement repetition or uncertainty information. This is a loss of reporting, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Matched image retrieval values in v1 Tables 1–2 and v2 Tables II/IV are unchanged. Substantial new results include V-DPPT rank-1 accuracies of 58.33% on HITSZ-VCM and 52.11% on BUPTCampus, cross-dataset video results, and robustness/reconstruction outcomes. Two image loss-ablation result rows are removed.

T1.justification: Section III-D introduces video-input notation and the temporal-mean sequence representation in Equation 9. The original ERM, MRB and aggregation equations remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal privacy guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: The contribution expands from an image-focused privacy benchmark to joint image/video evaluation with robustness and privacy testing. v2 adds data-scale claims and strengthens the conclusion from decentralized training not significantly affecting generalization to providing better generalization than centralized training.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking video behavior to temporal consistency and robustness/privacy behavior to diverse client representations. It interprets cross-dataset differences as evidence about data scale. New qualifications explicitly acknowledge the CI performance gap to centralized methods and the practical burden of requiring labeled surveillance data.

D1.justification: v2 documents video sequence lengths, batch construction, training epochs, exclusion of BUPTCampus auxiliary identities, and iDLG's Adam optimizer, learning rate and iteration count. Existing image implementation details and the code link remain. Parameter counts reported in v1 Table 2 are omitted from v2 Table IV.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions L2RW+ as an extension of the earlier CVPR work and distinguishes its new contributions. Related work expands to video VI-ReID, discussing MITML, IBAN, AuxNet, TF-CLIP and VLD, while new adversarial, corruption and gradient-inversion references broaden the research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized around the earlier benchmark and its extensions. The challenge taxonomy moves from methodology to related work; methodology and experiments separate image and video treatments. Visualization discussion is rewritten and expanded, with explicit limitations and structured future-work discussion.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an IEEE journal layout with author biographies, revises the overview diagram, and adds protocol, centralized-comparison, video and robustness tables. New challenge, video-processing, MRB and reconstruction figures accompany an expanded feature visualization. The retained entity-comparison table replaces its parameter-count column with protocol labels.

improvement.justification: Video component ablations test MRB's applicability beyond images, while centralized comparisons and explicit limitations clarify practical performance boundaries. These provide a net benefit. However, the ten-repeat disclosure disappears, and broad superiority claims exceed the mixed results in Tables VI and IX. New reporting errors also limit confidence: Table VI gives DNS rank-10 accuracy of 63.62% but rank-20 accuracy of 61.85%. The added evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
